findings.title: Late recognition and the binding word
findings.claim: The preceding scene makes the focus's conditional offer of guidance for every soul readable beside a plea made after seeing, hearing, and claiming certainty: the guidance could have arrived in time for right action, while the binding word meets the request to return as closure. This adds a temporal reading without denying that certainty has now arrived.
findings.mechanism: The supplied 32:12 scene moves from seeing and hearing to a request to be returned for fitting action and a claim of certainty; the focus immediately opens with a matching counterfactual and sets the clause of universal guidance against ḥaqqa al-qawl. Before this contact, universal guidance is an abstract hypothetical about present belief. With the late plea beside it, guidance also names the impossible retroactive conversion of certainty into timely action, and the binding word closes that alternate history. The focus's binding and utterance branches are registered; the six 32:12 root roles and their temporal relation are attributed to the HFT.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel why the hypothetical of guidance for every soul stands beside the adversative binding word: the speakers recognize and ask only after the point at which their requested return could change their deeds.
findings.containment: The focus still says that God could give every soul guidance and that the word from Him is binding before the oath about Hell. The temporal closure comes from the relation to 32:12; the same adjacency may chiefly contrast the human plea with divine power without specifying a moral timeline, and the supplied evidence leaves that alternative live.

findings.title: Guidance as remembered and embodied direction
findings.claim: The focus's guidance for each soul remains guidance, and the neighboring scenes let it carry a lived direction: forgetting the encounter is answered by reciprocal abandonment and experienced punishment, while being reminded is answered by bodily falling and submission.
findings.mechanism: The focus huda carries a registered direction-and-path facet. In 32:14 the judged speakers are told to taste for forgetting the encounter and hear that they have been forgotten; in 32:15 reminder precedes falling, prostration, and praise. This polarity lets guidance be read as a maintained remembrance that reorients body and relation, rather than information placed inside a self alone. Before the context contact, universal guidance is an abstract gift of correct information. After it, guidance also describes a remembered and enacted relation; a direct universal gift would make that responsive circuit automatic. The link from the adjacent outcomes to one guidance mechanism remains attributed to the HFT.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how the next scenes change the feel of the focus's hypothetical gift: guidance is not only something each soul would receive, but also a direction kept alive through remembrance and made visible in response.
findings.containment: The focus continues to say that God could give each soul guidance. The context adds an embodied, relational reading alongside that statement; the same verses can also be adjacent reward-and-punishment scenes without a shared guidance mechanism, and the packet does not choose between those explanations.

epistemic.reason: The focus huda branch and its core facet are registered, and exact Arabic anchors for 32:14 and 32:15 are supplied. Context segmentation, roots, branch roles, and the memory-to-posture circuit come from a legacy-unbound HFT trace; its own reader inference names the adjacent-scenes alternative.
